**Stay: 1/4. Switch: 3/8.**

**Staying.** Your door was chosen with no information, so it has the car with probability 1/4.

**Switching.** The car is behind one of the other 3 doors with probability 3/4. The host always opens a goat door among those 3 and never the car, so the opened door carries no probability of the car. That leaves the car behind one of the 2 unopened doors other than yours with probability 3/4 in total.

Those two doors are symmetric, so each has probability 3/8 of hiding the car. Switching to either one (chosen at random) wins with probability 3/8.

Switching therefore improves your chance from 1/4 to 3/8 (0.375 vs 0.25). The advantage is smaller than in the 3-door version, where switching wins with 2/3 versus 1/3, because the host's reveal removes only one of the three losing doors instead of the whole remaining set.
